questions.problem: Given the elliptic cone $\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9}={z}^{2},$ find its intercept with the $z$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
To find the $z$-intercept of the elliptic cone, we plug $x=0$ and $y=0$ into the equation and solve for $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{0}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{0}^{2}}{9} & ={z}^{2} \\ 0+0 & ={z}^{2} \\ {z}^{2} & =0 \\ z & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intercept with the $z$-axis is $(0,0,0)$ only.

questions.problem: Find the center of the elliptic cone $4(x-3)^{2}+5(y+2)^{2}=20(z-1)^{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The general equation of an elliptic cone with center at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ is

$$
\frac{(x-{x}_{0})^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-{y}_{0})^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=\frac{(z-{z}_{0})^{2}}{{c}^{2}}.
$$

To find the center, we rewrite our equation in standard form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4(x-3)^{2}+5(y+2)^{2} & =20(z-1)^{2} \\ \frac{(x-3)^{2}}{1/4}+\frac{(y+2)^{2}}{1/5} & =\frac{(z-1)^{2}}{1/20} \\ \frac{(x-3)^{2}}{1/4}+\frac{(y-(-2))^{2}}{1/5} & =\frac{(z-1)^{2}}{1/20}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of an elliptic cone that has its center at $(3,-2,1).$

questions.problem: Given the elliptic cone $\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}=\frac{{z}^{2}}{2},$ find its intercepts with the $y$-axis.
questions.worked_solution:
To find the $y$-intercepts of the elliptic cone, we plug $x=0$ and $z=0$ into the equation and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{0}^{2}}{8}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} & =\frac{{0}^{2}}{2} \\ 0+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} & =0 \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{4} & =0 \\ {y}^{2} & =0 \\ y & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intercept with the $y$-axis is $(0,0,0)$ only.

The general equation of an elliptic cone with center at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ is

$$
\frac{(x-{x}_{0})^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-{y}_{0})^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=\frac{(z-{z}_{0})^{2}}{{c}^{2}}.
$$

To find the center, we rewrite our equation in standard form, as follows:

questions.problem: Find the center of the elliptic cone $2(x+2)^{2}+3(y-1)^{2}={z}^{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The general equation of an elliptic cone with center at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ is

$$
\frac{(x-{x}_{0})^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{(y-{y}_{0})^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=\frac{(z-{z}_{0})^{2}}{{c}^{2}}.
$$

To find the center, we rewrite our equation in standard form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x+2)^{2}+3(y-1)^{2} & =(z-0)^{2} \\ \frac{(x+2)^{2}}{1/2}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{1/3} & =(z-0)^{2} \\ \frac{(x-(-2))^{2}}{1/2}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{1/3} & =(z-0)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of an elliptic cone that has its center at $(-2,1,0).$

questions.problem: Given that the intersection of the elliptic cone $3(x+4)^{2}+8{y}^{2}=12{z}^{2}$ and the plane $z=-2$ is an ellipse, what is the length of its major axis?
questions.worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the elliptic cone and the plane $z=-2,$ we substitute $z=-2$ into the equation of the elliptic cone, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}3(x+4)^{2}+8{y}^{2} & =12{z}^{2} \\ 3(x+4)^{2}+8{y}^{2} & =12(-2)^{2} \\ 3(x+4)^{2}+8{y}^{2} & =48 \\ \frac{(x+4)^{2}}{16}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{6} & =1 \\ \frac{(x+4)^{2}}{{4}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{(\sqrt{6})^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of an ellipse with a semi-major axis of length $a=4.$ Therefore, the major axis has length $2a=8.$

questions.problem: Given that the intersection of the elliptic cone $\frac{(x+4)^{2}}{16}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{8}={z}^{2}$ and the plane $z=-1$ is an ellipse, what is the length of its major axis?
questions.worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the elliptic cone and the plane $z=-1,$ we substitute $z=-1$ into the equation of the elliptic cone, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x+4)^{2}}{16}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{8} & ={z}^{2} \\ \frac{(x+4)^{2}}{16}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{8} & =(-1)^{2} \\ \frac{(x+4)^{2}}{16}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{8} & =1 \\ \frac{(x+4)^{2}}{{4}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{(2\sqrt{2})^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of an ellipse with a semi-major axis of length $a=4.$ Therefore, the major axis has length $2a=8.$

questions.problem: What is the trace in the $yz$-plane of the elliptic cone $\frac{{x}^{2}}{8}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}=(z-4)^{2}\,?$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the trace in the $yz$-plane, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the elliptic cone, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{0}^{2}}{8}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{4} & =(z-4)^{2} \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{2} & =(z-4)^{2} \\ \pm \frac{y}{2} & =z-4 \\ z & =\pm \frac{y}{2}+4\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us two lines in the $yz$-plane with equations $z=\pm \frac{y}{2}+4.$

questions.problem: Given that the intersection of the elliptic cone $\frac{(x+2)^{2}}{9}+\frac{(y-5)^{2}}{3}={z}^{2}$ and the plane $z=3$ is an ellipse, what is the length of its minor axis?
questions.worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the elliptic cone and the plane $z=3,$ we substitute $z=3$ into the equation of the elliptic cone, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(x+2)^{2}}{9}+\frac{(y-5)^{2}}{3}={z}^{2} \\ \frac{(x+2)^{2}}{9}+\frac{(y-5)^{2}}{3} & ={3}^{2} \\ \frac{(x+2)^{2}}{9}+\frac{(y-5)^{2}}{3} & =9 \\ \frac{(x+2)^{2}}{81}+\frac{(y-5)^{2}}{27} & =1 \\ \frac{(x+2)^{2}}{{9}^{2}}+\frac{(y-5)^{2}}{(3\sqrt{3})^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of an ellipse with a semi-minor axis of length $b=3\sqrt{3}.$ Therefore, the minor axis has length $2b=6\sqrt{3}.$

questions.problem: What is the trace in the $xz$-plane of the elliptic cone ${x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}=4{z}^{2}\,?$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the trace in the $xz$-plane, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the elliptic cone, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+4(0)^{2} & =4{z}^{2} \\ {x}^{2} & =4{z}^{2} \\ \pm x & =2z \\ z & =\pm \frac{x}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us two lines in the $xz$-plane with equations $z=\pm \frac{x}{2}.$

canonical_examples.problem: Given the elliptic cone $\dfrac{(x-2)^2}{4} + \dfrac{(y-2)^2}{2} = \dfrac{(z+1)^2}{3},$ find its intercepts with the $z$-axis.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To find the $z$-intercepts of the elliptic cone, we plug $x=0$ and $y=0$ into the equation and solve for $z\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(0-2)^{2}}{4}+\frac{(0-2)^{2}}{2} & =\frac{(z+1)^{2}}{3} \\ \frac{4}{4}+\frac{4}{2} & =\frac{(z+1)^{2}}{3} \\ 1+2 & =\frac{(z+1)^{2}}{3} \\ 3 & =\frac{(z+1)^{2}}{3} \\ 9 & =(z+1)^{2} \\ z+1 & =\pm 3 \\ z & =-1\pm 3 \\ z & =-4,2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the intercepts with the $z$-axis are $(0,0,-4)$ and $(0,0,2).$

canonical_examples.problem: What is the trace in the $xz$-plane of the elliptic cone $3x^2 +  4y ^2=12(z+3)^2\: ?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To find the trace in the $xz$-plane, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the elliptic cone, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+4\cdot {0}^{2} & =12(z+3)^{2} \\ 3{x}^{2} & =12(z+3)^{2} \\ {x}^{2} & =4(z+3)^{2} \\ \pm x & =2(z+3) \\ \pm \frac{x}{2} & =z+3 \\ z & =\pm \frac{x}{2}-3\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us two lines in the $xz$-plane with equations $z = \pm\dfrac{x}{2}-3.$
